questions.question: Which Australian mammal leaves behind droppings shaped like little cubes?
questions.explanation: Wombats produce roughly cube-shaped feces, formed by the unusual mechanical properties of their intestines.
questions.verificationNotes: The cubes form in the gut, not from a square-shaped exit.

questions.question: What disgusting problem became so severe in London in 1858 that it helped drive the construction of modern sewers?
questions.explanation: During the Great Stink, the reeking sewage-filled Thames made the need for new sewers politically urgent.

sources.title: The Great Stink - How the Victorians Transformed London to Solve the Problem of Waste

questions.verificationNotes: The smell was a symptom of an existing sanitation crisis, not the only cause of sewer reform.

questions.question: What was ketchup originally made from in some early Asian versions, long before tomatoes took over?
questions.explanation: Ketchup’s culinary ancestors included fermented fish sauces from Southeast Asia.

sources.title: There’s Something Fishy About the Ketchup You Put On Your Burgers

questions.verificationNotes: An origin for the word and sauce tradition, not a claim that all modern ketchup contains fish.

questions.question: Which planet has sunrises in the west because it spins in the opposite direction to most planets?
questions.explanation: Venus rotates retrograde, so the Sun would rise in the west and set in the east.
questions.verificationNotes: Compared with the usual prograde spin of planets; Uranus also has unusual spin.

questions.question: What spice might Danish friends pour over someone who is still single on their twenty-fifth birthday?
questions.explanation: A Danish birthday custom involves covering single twenty-five-year-olds with cinnamon.

sources.title: 11 weird Danish cultural traditions that only make sense to Danes

questions.verificationNotes: A documented custom, not an obligation for every Danish person.

questions.question: Which sea has no coastline and is instead defined by ocean currents?
questions.explanation: The Sargasso Sea in the Atlantic is bounded by circulating currents rather than land.
questions.verificationNotes: It is a sea in a gyre, not a conventional coastal inlet.

questions.question: What everyday behavior can spread from person to person just by seeing or thinking about it?
questions.explanation: Contagious yawning can be triggered by seeing, hearing, or thinking about another person yawning.
questions.verificationNotes: Not every person catches a yawn; susceptibility varies.

questions.question: What famous springy toy grew out of an engineer’s attempt to make equipment stable on ships?
questions.explanation: Richard James developed the Slinky after experimenting with springs intended to steady instruments on ships.
questions.verificationNotes: The toy arose from spring experiments, not an intentionally designed children’s game.

questions.question: What star-shaped flower smells like rotting meat to attract flies?
questions.explanation: The carrion plant (Stapelia gigantea) has striking star-shaped blooms that emit an odor like decaying flesh to lure fly pollinators.

sources.title: 16 weird plants that seem more supernatural than natural

questions.verificationNotes: Specifically carrion-flower species, rather than all flowers in deserts.

questions.question: What did people in Strasbourg reportedly keep doing uncontrollably during the strange outbreak of 1518?
questions.explanation: Historical reports describe a dancing mania in Strasbourg, with people moving for extended periods.

sources.title: What Was the Dancing Plague of 1518?

questions.verificationNotes: The cause and number of deaths are debated; only the documented dancing is asserted.

questions.question: What actually dries out frozen food and gives it so-called freezer burn?
questions.explanation: Poorly wrapped frozen food can lose water through sublimation, leaving dehydrated, discolored areas.
questions.verificationNotes: Freezer burn is dehydration and surface change, not combustion or bacteria.

questions.question: Which historical king gave his nickname to the wireless technology used by headphones and phones?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth was named for the Viking-age King Harald Bluetooth, associated with unifying Scandinavian groups.
questions.verificationNotes: The industry name began as a temporary codename and remained.

questions.question: What sea creature makes a protective sleeping bag out of its own mucus?
questions.explanation: Some parrotfish secrete a transparent mucus cocoon around themselves at night, which may help protect them from parasites.
questions.verificationNotes: Applies to certain parrotfish species, not every fish.

questions.question: Why did Victorian towns install tall metal pipes that rose above their streets and houses?
questions.explanation: Historic England describes Victorian stink pipes installed to release sewer gases safely above street level.
questions.verificationNotes: They were ventilation structures, not chimneys for heating homes.

questions.question: Which vegetable-like ingredient was commonly used to make British ketchup before tomatoes dominated?
questions.explanation: Historic British ketchup recipes included savory mushroom-based sauces and other non-tomato ingredients.

sources.title: A Brief (But Global) History of Ketchup

questions.verificationNotes: Some historical ketchups used walnuts as well; the question specifies a common example, not an exclusive ingredient.

questions.question: On which planet can the Sun briefly seem to rise, set, and then rise again?
questions.explanation: Mercury’s slow rotation combined with its changing orbital speed can make the apparent solar motion reverse at certain locations.
questions.verificationNotes: This effect occurs near specific longitudes, not everywhere on the planet.

questions.question: What piece of furniture do some Danes jump off at midnight on New Year’s Eve?
questions.explanation: A Danish New Year custom is to stand on a chair and jump down as the new year begins.

sources.title: 11 weird Danish cultural traditions that only make sense to Danes

questions.verificationNotes: Traditional symbolism about jumping into the new year, not universal behavior.

questions.question: What is the nickname for the point in the ocean farther from land than anywhere else?
questions.explanation: Point Nemo is the oceanic pole of inaccessibility, in the remote South Pacific.
questions.verificationNotes: This refers to a specific geographical location rather than a fictional submarine captain.

questions.question: What natural urge can feel stronger if someone specifically tells you not to do it?
questions.explanation: Experiments found that instructions to resist yawning could increase people’s reported urge to yawn.

sources.title: A Neural Basis for Contagious Yawning

questions.verificationNotes: This concerns the urge to yawn, not necessarily the number of completed yawns.

questions.question: What unusual role did American soldiers find for the Slinky during the Vietnam War?
questions.explanation: Metal Slinkys were sometimes stretched out as improvised radio antennas during the Vietnam War.
questions.verificationNotes: An improvised field use, not the toy’s original purpose.

questions.question: What kind of plant can find a host using chemical smells instead of relying on green leaves?
questions.explanation: Dodder is a parasitic vine with little chlorophyll; seedlings detect host-plant chemical cues as they grow.

sources.title: 16 weird plants that seem more supernatural than natural

questions.verificationNotes: The smell refers to plant volatile chemicals rather than a human-like sense of smell.

questions.question: What contagious-sounding behavior disrupted schools around Lake Victoria in 1962?
questions.explanation: A widely reported outbreak of prolonged laughing episodes affected students in Tanganyika, now Tanzania.

sources.title: 7 Mysterious Mass Illnesses That Defied Explanation

questions.verificationNotes: Usually interpreted as a mass psychogenic event; mechanism not established as infectious.

questions.question: What is released when you cut an onion that makes your eyes water?
questions.explanation: Cutting onion cells releases chemicals that form a volatile tear-producing irritant.

sources.title: Why does chopping an onion make you cry?

questions.verificationNotes: The specific irritant is syn-propanethial-S-oxide; cutting releases its precursors.

questions.question: What old alphabet inspired the shape of the Bluetooth wireless logo?
questions.explanation: The logo combines runes representing the initials H and B of Harald Bluetooth.
questions.verificationNotes: Two Younger Futhark runes form a bind rune, not arbitrary zigzags.

questions.question: Which animal has three hearts and blue blood?
questions.explanation: Octopuses have two hearts pumping blood to the gills and one for the rest of the body; copper-based hemocyanin makes their blood blue.

sources.title: Ten Wild Facts About Octopuses: They Have Three Hearts, Big Brains and Blue Blood

questions.verificationNotes: Question asks for a familiar example, not a claim of uniqueness.

questions.question: During wartime clothing rationing, what decoration on jeans did Levi’s sometimes paint on instead of sewing?
questions.explanation: Levi’s painted its curved arcuate pocket decoration on some wartime jeans to save thread.
questions.verificationNotes: The painted lines mimicked the familiar stitched pattern; wartime restrictions motivated the change.

questions.question: What animal was once the source of a natural flavoring occasionally used in vanilla-like foods?
questions.explanation: Castoreum, a secretion from beavers, has a history of use in perfumery and some food flavorings.

sources.title: 9 Fascinating Facts About North America’s Master Builder, the Beaver

questions.verificationNotes: Rare in modern foods; avoid claiming vanilla ice cream routinely contains castoreum.

questions.question: Which planet rolls around the Sun almost on its side?
questions.explanation: Uranus has an axial tilt of about 98 degrees, making its rotation axis point roughly along its orbital plane.
questions.verificationNotes: Sideways refers to axial tilt, not a literal wheel rolling on a surface.

questions.question: What do children hit at Denmark’s Fastelavn festival instead of hitting a piñata?
questions.explanation: Costumed children strike a barrel with sticks until it breaks and releases sweets.

sources.title: 11 weird Danish cultural traditions that only make sense to Danes

questions.verificationNotes: Historically live cats were sometimes involved; the modern version uses candy.

questions.question: What single letter is also the complete name of a village in France?
questions.explanation: The commune of Y in northern France is famous for its one-letter name.
questions.verificationNotes: French commune name, not an abbreviation for a longer city name.

questions.question: What costumed animal did many viewers miss while concentrating on counting basketball passes?
questions.explanation: The classic inattentional-blindness demonstration included a gorilla-suited person passing through a basketball scene.

sources.title: Researching the Extremes of Visual Perception

questions.verificationNotes: Participants were concentrating on counting passes; many but not all missed it.

questions.question: What annoying thing that stuck to a dog helped inspire the invention of Velcro?
questions.explanation: George de Mestral studied hooked burrs caught in fur and clothing, inspiring hook-and-loop fasteners.
questions.verificationNotes: The natural hooks, not an actual dog hair material, inspired the design.

questions.question: What does a ghost plant take nourishment from instead of making its own food in sunlight?
questions.explanation: Ghost plants lack chlorophyll and acquire carbon via networks of fungi associated with other plants.

sources.title: 16 weird plants that seem more supernatural than natural

questions.verificationNotes: The plant is mycoheterotrophic; fungi are the immediate nutritional connection.

questions.question: Which mysterious creature did frightened Delhi residents report seeing during a 2001 panic?
questions.explanation: A wave of reports about a supposed monkey-like attacker caused panic in Delhi.

sources.title: 7 Mysterious Mass Illnesses That Defied Explanation

questions.verificationNotes: Reports and panic were real; existence of an actual attacker was unverified.

questions.question: What living creature can act as a makeshift thermometer if you count its chirps?
questions.explanation: For some crickets, the frequency of chirping changes with air temperature and can be used as a rough estimate.

sources.title: Can you tell the temperature by listening to the chirping of a cricket?

questions.verificationNotes: The approximation is species- and temperature-dependent, not a calibrated universal rule.

questions.question: What comedy group inspired the name of the Python programming language?
questions.explanation: Guido van Rossum named Python after Monty Python, not after the snake.
questions.verificationNotes: A naming inspiration explicitly stated by the official Python documentation.

questions.question: What animal can deliver venom through spurs on its back legs?
questions.explanation: Adult male platypuses have venom-producing glands connected to spurs on their hind legs.
questions.verificationNotes: The venomous spurs are a characteristic of males; females do not normally have functional adult spurs.

questions.question: What surprisingly ordinary object was the tiny extra pocket on early blue jeans meant to hold?
questions.explanation: The small fifth pocket of jeans originally served as a handy watch pocket.
questions.verificationNotes: The historical purpose differs from its many modern uses.

questions.question: What plant originally supplied the gooey ingredient that gave marshmallow sweets their name?
questions.explanation: Older marshmallow treats used gummy extracts from the root of the marsh mallow plant.
questions.verificationNotes: Most modern marshmallows use gelatin rather than mallow-root extract.

questions.question: What color can a sunset appear on Mars, near the setting Sun?
questions.explanation: Fine dust in the Martian atmosphere can make the sky near sunset appear bluish, unlike common Earth sunsets.
questions.verificationNotes: Color is especially near the Sun, not uniformly blue across every sunset.

questions.question: What prize is given to the winners of Finland’s famous wife-carrying competition?
questions.answer: Beer equal to the carried person’s weight
questions.explanation: The well-known wife-carrying championship awards beer equivalent to the carried wife’s weight.
questions.verificationNotes: Prize description belongs to the organized competition; event rules may evolve.

questions.question: On which Indonesian island can visitors find a volcano famous for eerie blue sulfur flames?
questions.explanation: The Ijen volcanic area on Java is known for vivid blue burning sulfur gas at night.
questions.verificationNotes: Java is the island; Indonesia is the country, and Kawah Ijen is the volcano.

questions.question: What detail made volunteers rate the very same wine as tasting better in a brain-scanning study?
questions.explanation: Volunteers rated identical wines as more pleasant when told they cost more; researchers also observed changes in activity in a brain region associated with pleasure.

sources.title: Marketing actions can modulate neural representations of experienced pleasantness
sources.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences / PubMed

sources.title: Wine Study Shows Price Influences Perception

questions.verificationNotes: The price was experimentally manipulated, and the reported effect pertains to participants in this study; it does not prove all wine drinkers are affected.

questions.question: The name Velcro combines French words for velvet and what other thing?
questions.explanation: Velcro derives from velours and crochet, French for velvet and hook.
questions.verificationNotes: Crochet here refers to a hook, not the English name for needlework alone.

questions.question: What animal’s droppings are an important source of nutrients for some tropical pitcher plants?
questions.explanation: Some Nepenthes pitcher plants reward tree shrews with nectar and collect their feces as nutrients.

sources.title: Carnivorous plants: the meat-eaters of the plant world

questions.verificationNotes: Describes a particular pitcher-plant adaptation, not all carnivorous plants.

questions.question: What happened over Siberia in 1908 that flattened a vast forest without leaving a typical impact crater?
questions.answer: An asteroid exploded in the atmosphere
questions.explanation: The Tunguska blast is understood as an atmospheric explosion from a cosmic body, flattening forest without a clear impact crater.

sources.title: 115 Years Ago: The Tunguska Asteroid Impact Event

questions.verificationNotes: Best explanation is an airburst; the exact nature of the object remains studied.

questions.question: What oily substance helps planes write smoky messages high in the sky?
questions.explanation: Traditional skywriting systems inject paraffin oil into hot exhaust to make visible white smoke.

sources.title: How do skywriting and skytyping work?

questions.verificationNotes: Applies to smoke skywriting, not laser or searchlight projection.

questions.question: What two-word holiday greeting was sent in the first SMS text message in 1992?
questions.explanation: The first widely cited SMS message in 1992 read Merry Christmas.

sources.title: 25 years since the world’s first text message

questions.verificationNotes: Sent from a computer to a mobile phone, not a normal phone-to-phone exchange.

questions.question: Which tiny creature wears its old heads stacked on top of its new one?
questions.explanation: The gum-leaf skeletoniser caterpillar retains its cast-off head capsules as a strange tower or hat.

sources.title: Curious collectors and hoarders of the animal world

questions.verificationNotes: Refers to the caterpillar stage, not an adult moth.

questions.question: What food-related substance set off a deadly industrial explosion at a Minneapolis mill in 1878?
questions.explanation: Fine airborne flour dust ignited at the Washburn A Mill, causing a devastating explosion.

sources.title: Four Deadly Disasters Caused by Food

questions.verificationNotes: Dust suspended in air is explosive under the right conditions; sacks of flour do not ordinarily explode.

questions.question: What was candy corn marketed as under a farm-themed name in the nineteenth century?
questions.explanation: The Goelitz company sold candy corn under the label Chicken Feed in the late 1800s.

sources.title: Candy Corn Hasn’t Changed Since the 19th Century

questions.verificationNotes: A historical brand label, not actual chicken food.

questions.question: What liquid fills the lakes and seas on Saturn’s moon Titan?
questions.explanation: Titan has stable surface bodies of liquid methane and ethane in its very cold climate.
questions.verificationNotes: Not lakes of liquid water; both hydrocarbons may be present.

questions.question: At a Finnish festival, what imaginary instrument do competitors pretend to perform with?
questions.explanation: The Air Guitar World Championships in Oulu feature performances with no real instrument.
questions.verificationNotes: The competition explicitly embraces imaginary playing and performance.

questions.question: Which Pacific island country is famous for hundreds of limestone islands shaped like mushrooms?
questions.explanation: Palau’s Rock Islands are a UNESCO-listed group of limestone islands with distinctive mushroom-like outlines.
questions.verificationNotes: Refers to the Rock Islands Southern Lagoon, not every island in Palau.

questions.question: What color did participants in one study tend to associate with calming rather than stimulating pills?
questions.explanation: In a placebo-color study, blue pills were more often classified with sedating effects than warm-colored pills.

sources.title: Classification of placebo drugs: effect of color

questions.verificationNotes: Concerns expectations and color associations, not real effects of a medicinal ingredient.

questions.question: What kitchen coating was discovered by accident during a search for a new refrigerant?
questions.explanation: Roy Plunkett unexpectedly found polytetrafluoroethylene while studying tetrafluoroethylene for refrigerants.
questions.verificationNotes: Teflon is the trade name for PTFE; discovery preceded its nonstick cookware use.

questions.question: Which flying mammal is invited to sleep inside some pitcher plants in exchange for fertilizer?
questions.explanation: Certain pitcher plants provide roosting space for small bats, benefiting from nutrients in bat droppings.

sources.title: Carnivorous plants: the meat-eaters of the plant world

questions.verificationNotes: The plant is adapted for small roosting bats, not capturing them as prey.

questions.question: What food was reported falling from the sky over Marksville, Louisiana, in 1947?
questions.explanation: A documented 1947 local report described fish falling from the sky near Marksville, Louisiana.

sources.title: Can it rain frogs, fish, and other objects?

questions.verificationNotes: The rainfall report is witnessed; the exact atmospheric transport mechanism is not directly established.

questions.question: What can briefly happen to tiny gas pockets in your joints when you crack your knuckles?
questions.explanation: Joint popping is linked in part to rapid changes involving gas-filled cavities in joint fluid.

sources.title: What causes the noise when you crack a joint?

questions.verificationNotes: Several mechanisms explain different joint sounds; no one mechanism explains all clicks.

questions.question: What industrial products were QR codes originally designed to help track?
questions.explanation: DENSO Wave developed QR codes for efficient tracking of automotive components in manufacturing.
questions.verificationNotes: Original use case, not the later smartphone link-sharing use.

questions.question: Which bird is notorious for decorating its courtship display with blue objects?
questions.explanation: Male satin bowerbirds arrange blue items around their bowers to attract mates.

sources.title: Curious collectors and hoarders of the animal world

questions.verificationNotes: The blue objects decorate a bower; they are not used to build a nest for eggs.

questions.question: What alcoholic drink flooded part of London after a huge vat collapsed in 1814?
questions.explanation: A porter vat collapsed at the Horse Shoe Brewery, sending a destructive torrent of beer through a London neighborhood.

sources.title: This 1814 Beer Flood Killed Eight People

questions.verificationNotes: The incident involved porter beer rather than a river or water main.

questions.question: What root is often used as the main ingredient in imitation wasabi served with sushi?
questions.explanation: Much commercially sold imitation wasabi is based on horseradish with mustard and coloring.
questions.verificationNotes: Real wasabi is a different though related plant; products vary.

questions.question: What substance makes the hills on Pluto able to float like icebergs on a frozen plain?
questions.explanation: Rigid water-ice blocks on Pluto can float in a softer frozen-nitrogen matrix, creating hill-like features.
questions.verificationNotes: The floating is through denser frozen nitrogen, not a lake of liquid nitrogen.

questions.question: What unexpected soup is traditionally served on birthdays in South Korea?
questions.explanation: Miyeokguk, a seaweed soup, is traditionally eaten on Korean birthdays, reflecting its association with mothers and childbirth.
questions.verificationNotes: An established cultural tradition, not a claim that every person follows it for every birthday.

questions.question: Which Philippine volcano sits inside a lake and has a crater lake of its own?
questions.explanation: Taal Volcano occupies an island within Taal Lake, and volcanic craters have hosted lakes on the island.

sources.title: The Historic Towns and Landscape of Taal Volcano and its Caldera Lake

questions.verificationNotes: The nested lake arrangement has changed during eruptions; wording describes established geography.

questions.question: What sense can change the syllable someone thinks they hear, even when the recorded sound stays the same?
questions.explanation: The McGurk effect shows that incongruent lip movements can alter auditory speech perception.
questions.verificationNotes: A demonstrable audio-visual illusion, not a universal effect for all speakers or sounds.

questions.question: What office product became possible because an adhesive proved surprisingly weak?
questions.explanation: A 3M researcher developed a low-tack repositionable adhesive that later became useful on Post-it Notes.

sources.title: One scientist, good. Many scientists, even better.

questions.verificationNotes: The adhesive did not stick permanently, which made the product useful.

questions.question: What is the glowing blue “lava” seen at Indonesia’s Ijen volcano actually made by?
questions.explanation: Ijen’s striking blue flames come from burning sulfurous gases, rather than molten blue rock.
questions.verificationNotes: The flames can be blue; the actual lava or molten rock is not blue.

questions.question: What amphibians were reported raining on a Serbian town in 2005?
questions.explanation: Reports from Serbia in 2005 described frogs falling during unusual weather.

sources.title: Can it rain frogs, fish, and other objects?

questions.verificationNotes: Historical eyewitness reporting, not laboratory proof of exactly how the animals were lifted.

questions.question: Which part of the body may fail to wrinkle normally in water when its nerves are damaged?
questions.explanation: Water-immersion wrinkling of fingers involves nerve-controlled blood vessel changes, and nerve damage can reduce it.

sources.title: Why do fingers and toes wrinkle in the bathtub?

questions.verificationNotes: Wrinkling has multiple contributing mechanisms; nerve response is important.

questions.question: Which surprisingly delicate packaged product was an early general-commercial use of QR codes?
questions.explanation: DENSO reports that contact lens packaging was QR codes’ first general commercial product application.
questions.verificationNotes: Manufacturer’s documented historical example; production tracking predates it.

questions.question: Which insect uses dead ants to seal up its babies’ chambers?
questions.explanation: The bone-house wasp was reported using dead ant bodies in a protective vestibule around its brood cells.

sources.title: Curious collectors and hoarders of the animal world

questions.verificationNotes: Behavior is species-specific, not typical of wasps generally.

questions.question: What sticky food ingredient flooded a Boston neighborhood in 1919?
questions.explanation: A large storage tank failed and unleashed a deadly wave of molasses through Boston’s North End.

sources.title: Without Warning, Molasses Surged Over Boston 100 Years Ago

questions.verificationNotes: The event was a real industrial disaster, not a joke about slow-moving liquid.

questions.question: Which way of growing is one possible reason the grapefruit got its name?
questions.explanation: Grapefruits often grow in clusters on trees, somewhat like bunches of grapes; this is a commonly proposed explanation for the name.

sources.title: How did the grapefruit get its name? It doesn’t look like a grape.

questions.verificationNotes: The Library of Congress gives this as a believed etymology and notes another theory based on immature fruit; it is not a settled origin.

questions.question: Which playwright inspired the names of several moons orbiting Uranus?
questions.explanation: Uranian moons include characters from plays by William Shakespeare, with others named from Alexander Pope.
questions.verificationNotes: This describes the naming theme, not a specific count of moons.

questions.question: What craft do competitors perform while headbanging at Finland’s heavy-metal championship?
questions.explanation: The Heavy Metal Knitting World Championships combine knitting with energetic heavy-metal performance.

sources.title: Weirdly wonderful competitions and events: 12 quirky reasons to visit Finland

questions.verificationNotes: The craft is performed as part of a specific novelty competition.

questions.question: Which Australian island gives its name to a giant stick insect once thought extinct?
questions.explanation: The Lord Howe Island stick insect survived on the nearby rocky islet of Ball’s Pyramid and was rediscovered after being thought extinct.
questions.verificationNotes: The species takes its common name from Lord Howe Island; the rediscovered wild insects lived on Ball’s Pyramid, not necessarily on the main island.

questions.question: What object can people briefly feel is part of their own body when it is stroked in sync with a hidden hand?
questions.explanation: Matching touches to a fake hand and a hidden real hand can create an illusion of owning the fake hand.

sources.title: Body Representation Differs in Children and Adults

questions.verificationNotes: The feeling is temporary and depends on experimental conditions.

questions.question: What snack reportedly popped during early tests that led to microwave cooking?
questions.explanation: Early microwave experiments included popping corn kernels using radar-related magnetron energy.

sources.title: Cook Today . . . Tomorrow’s Way
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

questions.verificationNotes: Popcorn was a test observation, not the sole origin of microwave cooking.

questions.question: What everyday loose material can make an eerie musical hum as it slides down a dune?
questions.explanation: Sand avalanches in the dunes can generate a deep booming or humming sound when grains move together.

sources.title: Geology - Great Sand Dunes National Park & Preserve

questions.verificationNotes: The sound depends on suitable dry sand and motion; not every step makes music.

questions.question: What gas burst from Cameroon’s Lake Nyos in 1986 and suffocated people in nearby villages?
questions.explanation: Lake Nyos released a dense cloud of carbon dioxide which displaced breathable air.
questions.verificationNotes: This was a limnic gas-release disaster, not ordinary toxic volcanic ash.

questions.question: What supposedly stops during a sneeze, according to a widespread myth, but actually does not?
questions.explanation: Sneezing can briefly change chest pressure and heart rhythm, but the heart does not stop beating.

sources.title: Does your heart stop when you sneeze?

questions.verificationNotes: Corrects the myth; the heart continues functioning during a sneeze.

questions.question: What did the world’s first website primarily explain to visitors?
questions.explanation: CERN says the first website described the World Wide Web project and how to use it.
questions.verificationNotes: The first website was project documentation, not a news service or shop.

questions.question: What small insect-like hunter has venomous pincers but no stinging tail?
questions.explanation: Pseudoscorpions are tiny arachnids that use venom glands associated with their pincers to capture small prey.
questions.verificationNotes: Unlike true scorpions, pseudoscorpions have no scorpion tail.

questions.question: What early frozen dessert container was shaped using a metal tool called a mandrel?
questions.explanation: A Smithsonian collection item preserves a mandrel used for shaping cone-like wafer containers.

sources.title: Doumar Ice Cream Cone Mandrel, 1920s
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

questions.verificationNotes: The tool shows cone-making technology, not a claim about a single undisputed inventor.

questions.question: What flavor could an eighteenth-century ice cream shaped like an artichoke use to make it look green?
questions.explanation: Historical molded ice creams were sometimes flavored and colored to resemble vegetables; pistachio could make an artichoke shape green.

sources.title: The Lost Art of Molding Ice Cream Into Eagles, Tugboats and Pineapples

questions.verificationNotes: An attested historical example rather than a universal artichoke-ice-cream recipe.

questions.question: What chemical makes ordinary black pepper particularly irritating to your nose?
questions.explanation: Piperine in black pepper irritates nasal membranes, which can trigger a sneeze.

sources.title: Why does pepper make you sneeze?

questions.verificationNotes: The question refers to pepper spice, not hot chili peppers and capsaicin.

questions.question: What fruit is thrown by the truckload during a summer festival in Buñol, Spain?
questions.explanation: La Tomatina in Buñol is a mass tomato-throwing celebration.
questions.verificationNotes: A regulated festival event, not a general annual custom throughout Spain.

questions.question: In Yellowstone, what unusually hot feature once flowed straight into the Gardner River?
questions.explanation: The Boiling River was a naturally heated stream flowing into the Gardner River; its area was reshaped in the 2022 flood.

sources.title: How the 2022 Yellowstone flood affected a monitoring site on the Gardner River

questions.verificationNotes: A historical Yellowstone feature; public access and the streambed changed after 2022.

questions.question: What unpleasant thing did some participants choose to give themselves instead of sitting alone doing nothing?
questions.explanation: In laboratory experiments, some people administered mild electric shocks to themselves rather than simply think quietly.

sources.title: We dislike being alone with our thoughts

questions.verificationNotes: Voluntary mild experimental shocks; do not generalize to all participants.

questions.question: What small clothing fastener did Walter Hunt devise while trying to pay off a debt?
questions.explanation: Walter Hunt worked out a spring-clasp pin design in 1849 while trying to clear a personal debt.
questions.verificationNotes: His design improved earlier pin concepts; it was not the first pin ever made.

questions.question: What surprising shape do the ripe white berries of the doll’s-eye plant resemble?
questions.explanation: The white fruit has a dark central spot and resembles tiny eyeballs on red stalks.

sources.title: 16 weird plants that seem more supernatural than natural

questions.verificationNotes: The plant is poisonous to people; this is its appearance, not its function.

questions.question: What natural phenomenon did a 2017 flash stretch across roughly 829 kilometers of the United States?
questions.explanation: Meteorological analysis identified an enormous 2017 lightning megaflash stretching about 829 kilometers.
questions.verificationNotes: Fixed historical measurement, not a claim it will forever remain a record.

questions.question: What property of your finger allows a modern capacitive touchscreen to sense a tap?
questions.explanation: Many modern touchscreens detect changes in an electrical field caused by a conductive finger.

sources.title: How does a touch screen work?

questions.verificationNotes: Applies to capacitive touchscreens, not all resistive or pressure-based screens.

questions.question: What communal kitchen item did an early webcam at Cambridge University continuously monitor?
questions.explanation: Researchers created a camera feed so they could check whether a shared coffee pot had coffee before walking to it.

sources.title: The Antiques Code Show
sources.publisher: University of Cambridge Department of Computer Science and Technology

questions.verificationNotes: Initially local network monitoring in 1991; subsequently connected to the web.

questions.question: Which lizard turns its ribs into something resembling wings to glide between trees?
questions.explanation: Draco lizards extend elongated ribs to stretch skin into gliding surfaces.

sources.title: Fantastic flyers: 10 animals that fly in surprising ways

questions.verificationNotes: They glide rather than fly by flapping wings; flying dragon is a common name for Draco.

questions.question: What edible accident allegedly alerted a nineteenth-century chemist to the sweetness of saccharin?
questions.explanation: Historical accounts say Constantin Fahlberg noticed an unusually sweet taste while eating after lab work, leading to saccharin research.
questions.verificationNotes: The bread detail comes from the documented discovery anecdote, not proof of a controlled experiment.

questions.question: What shape are fortune cookies when first removed from the oven, before the slip goes inside?
questions.explanation: Fortune cookies start as flat baked rounds and are folded around the paper while still warm and pliable.

sources.title: How do fortunes get inside of fortune cookies?

questions.verificationNotes: This is the process before the familiar crescent hardens.

questions.question: What is the main reason a bright-colored shirt can fade after too much exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet and visible light can alter chemical bonds in dyes, leading to photodegradation and color loss.

sources.title: Why does ultraviolet light cause color to fade?

questions.verificationNotes: The cause is chemical change, not simply dye physically leaking out of fabric.

questions.question: What root vegetable is carved into elaborate Christmas displays in Oaxaca, Mexico?
questions.explanation: Oaxaca’s Night of the Radishes features elaborate carvings using oversized radishes.
questions.verificationNotes: The specialty radishes are grown for the festival; they are not tiny salad garnishes.

questions.question: Which famous Wyoming rock formation was traditionally called Bear Lodge by many Indigenous peoples?
questions.explanation: The rock now officially called Devils Tower has Indigenous names often translated as Bear Lodge.

sources.title: About the Name - Devils Tower National Monument

questions.verificationNotes: The origins of the newer Devil name are contested; Bear Lodge is well documented.

questions.question: What can start playing repeatedly in your mind after music before bed, sometimes disturbing sleep?
questions.explanation: Studies linked involuntary musical imagery after bedtime listening with disturbed sleep.

sources.title: Bedtime Music, Involuntary Musical Imagery, and Sleep

questions.verificationNotes: The effect depends on music and individuals; it does not mean all music harms sleep.

questions.question: What bathroom item did Marion Donovan cut up while developing an early waterproof diaper cover?
questions.explanation: Donovan experimented with waterproof diaper covers using material from shower curtains.
questions.verificationNotes: Her later commercial design used more suitable fabric rather than permanently using shower curtains.

questions.question: What kind of animal can be fooled by the false “windows” inside a cobra lily plant?
questions.explanation: Cobra lilies have translucent areas that confuse prey insects after they enter a trap.

sources.title: 16 weird plants that seem more supernatural than natural

questions.verificationNotes: The false windows are part of a carnivorous plant trap, not a true building-like window.

questions.question: What weather phenomenon over South America lasted more than seventeen seconds during a 2020 event?
questions.explanation: A 2020 lightning megaflash over South America lasted around 17.1 seconds.
questions.verificationNotes: A recorded atmospheric flash, not continuous thunder or an electrical grid outage.

questions.question: What causes a tiny electric shock after you walk across a carpet and touch a metal handle?
questions.explanation: Friction and contact can transfer charge to your body, releasing it abruptly when you touch a conductor.
questions.verificationNotes: The spark is an electrostatic discharge, not a continuous mains current.

questions.question: Which punctuation symbol did an early email pioneer select to separate usernames from computers?
questions.explanation: Ray Tomlinson chose the at sign in early network email addresses to distinguish the user from the host.
questions.verificationNotes: Specifically the user@host convention, not the original invention of the @ symbol.

questions.question: Which snake can flatten its body and glide from one tree to another?
questions.explanation: The paradise tree snake can launch from trees and flatten its body to control a glide.

sources.title: Fantastic flyers: 10 animals that fly in surprising ways

questions.verificationNotes: Gliding is controlled aerial motion, not powered flight.

questions.question: Whose centuries-old skeleton was discovered beneath a car park in Leicester in 2012?
questions.explanation: University of Leicester archaeologists found a skeleton under the former Greyfriars car park and confirmed by scientific tests that it belonged to the English king Richard III.

sources.title: Discovery of King Richard III’s remains named as one of the decade’s extraordinary discoveries

questions.verificationNotes: Discovered in 2012; identification confirmed by the university in February 2013. The archaeological context was a former friary.

questions.question: Despite their name, what type of legume are black-eyed peas usually classified as?
questions.explanation: Black-eyed peas are cowpeas, usually described as beans within the legume family.
questions.verificationNotes: Bean and pea are both common legume labels; the source explicitly describes them as beans.

questions.question: In an ordinary sink, what matters more to the water’s swirl than which hemisphere you live in?
questions.answer: How the water enters and the drain’s shape
questions.explanation: Small drain vortices depend on initial flow and sink geometry; Earth’s rotation is too weak to determine a typical sink’s swirl.

sources.title: Does water go down the drain counterclockwise in the northern hemisphere and clockwise in the southern hemisphere?

questions.verificationNotes: Refutes the common hemispheric bathtub myth, not the Coriolis effect in large weather systems.

questions.question: What do masked visitors representing deities scold children for in a traditional Japanese New Year ritual?
questions.explanation: Raiho-shin performers visit homes in frightening masks to encourage good behavior and admonish laziness.

sources.title: Raiho-shin, ritual visits of deities in masks and costumes

questions.verificationNotes: These are regional rituals, not a practice of every family across Japan.

questions.question: What seaweed keeps itself afloat using tiny gas-filled structures that look a little like berries?
questions.explanation: Floating Sargassum has gas-filled bladders that provide buoyancy on the sea surface.
questions.verificationNotes: The berry-like spheres are floats, not edible berries.

questions.question: What makes an odd-colored item easier to remember than similar items in a list?
questions.explanation: The distinctiveness effect describes improved recall for an item that differs sharply from surrounding items.
questions.verificationNotes: The exact mechanism depends on context; distinctiveness is relative to the comparison set.

questions.question: What mode of public transport inspired an early windshield wiper after the inventor watched its driver struggle?
questions.explanation: Mary Anderson saw a trolley driver trying to clear snow and rain from the front window and developed a wiper idea.
questions.verificationNotes: Refers to Anderson’s patented wiper design, not every previous cleaning device.

questions.question: What underwater plant snaps shut a trap much like a Venus flytrap?
questions.explanation: The aquatic waterwheel plant, Aldrovanda, has small snap traps that close on underwater prey.

sources.title: Carnivorous plants: the meat-eaters of the plant world

questions.verificationNotes: It is a different plant from the terrestrial Venus flytrap.

questions.question: What terrifying type of whirlwind appeared during California’s 2018 Carr Fire?
questions.explanation: The Carr Fire generated a fire vortex with winds estimated at tornado strength, documented by weather scientists.

sources.title: Ask the scientist: How can the weather spark and spread wildfires?

questions.verificationNotes: The source describes a fire-generated vortex, distinct from common small fire whirls.

questions.question: What breakfast food is often said to cook on hot pavement, though ordinary pavement rarely gets hot enough?
questions.explanation: The popular sidewalk-frying demonstration usually fails because pavement does not supply enough sustained heat.

sources.title: Is it possible to fry an egg on the sidewalk if it’s hot enough?

questions.verificationNotes: The source says theoretically possible but normally impractical on real sidewalks.

questions.question: Which home communications technology was patented in the 1840s, long before the telephone became common?
questions.explanation: The basic facsimile idea received an early patent in 1843, long before modern office fax machines.

sources.title: Faxed: the rise and fall of the fax machine

questions.verificationNotes: The historical patent was for an early fax concept, not a late twentieth-century office device.

questions.question: Which animal has eyes so large that each is comparable in size to its brain?
questions.explanation: A tarsier’s enormous eyes are each about as large as its brain and help it see in dim light.
questions.verificationNotes: Comparison is by size/volume, not a precise weight equality.

questions.question: What did Clarence Birdseye observe freezing rapidly in the Arctic that inspired his commercial food-freezing work?
questions.explanation: Birdseye watched fish freeze quickly in the cold Labrador climate and learned that fast freezing preserved quality.
questions.verificationNotes: He did not invent the basic practice of freezing food, only key commercial techniques.

questions.question: What makes turkey legs darker than turkey breast meat?
questions.explanation: Turkey leg muscles are used more and contain more myoglobin, giving them a darker appearance.

sources.title: Why do turkeys have dark and white meat?

questions.verificationNotes: Activity and muscle pigment, not the bird being cooked longer.

questions.question: What tiny objects inside fireworks are deliberately arranged to draw shapes in the sky?
questions.explanation: Fireworks contain burning pellets called stars; arranging them makes patterns when shells burst.
questions.verificationNotes: Uses conventional pyrotechnic meaning of stars, not astronomical stars.

questions.question: What do guests clang at some Danish weddings to demand the couple kiss while standing on chairs?
questions.explanation: In a described Danish wedding custom, clanging utensils prompts newlyweds to stand on chairs and kiss.

sources.title: 11 weird Danish cultural traditions that only make sense to Danes

questions.verificationNotes: Stomping feet instead prompts a kiss under the table, a different signal.

questions.question: Which continent contains enormous areas classified as a desert despite being covered in ice?
questions.explanation: Much of Antarctica is a polar desert because precipitation is extremely low.

sources.title: Snow
sources.publisher: National Snow and Ice Data Center

questions.verificationNotes: Desert classification depends on precipitation, not whether a place is hot.

questions.question: What warm object made participants in a psychology experiment report feeling socially closer to others?
questions.explanation: In reported experiments, holding warm rather than cold drinks affected ratings of social closeness.
questions.verificationNotes: A context-specific experimental finding, not a guarantee a hot drink makes people kinder.

questions.question: What accidental electronics mistake helped inspire a wearable heart-regulating device?
questions.explanation: Wilson Greatbatch fitted the wrong resistor in a circuit and noticed pulses useful for an implantable pacemaker.
questions.verificationNotes: It was one step in engineering the later clinically successful device.

questions.question: What material replaces the original wood when a tree becomes petrified?
questions.explanation: During petrification, minerals occupy or replace organic wood tissues, leaving a stone-like fossil.
questions.verificationNotes: Petrified is a geological fossilization process; wood was originally organic.

questions.question: What mode of transport did a runner secretly use during part of the 1904 Olympic marathon?
questions.explanation: Fred Lorz rode part of the St. Louis marathon course in an automobile before returning to run.

sources.title: Shortcuts to Gold: 9 Cheaters in Olympic History

questions.verificationNotes: He was disqualified after the deception was discovered.

questions.question: What specialized optical object lets lighthouse lamps send a concentrated beam many miles out to sea?
questions.explanation: Lighthouses use special lens systems to focus light into powerful, narrow beams.

sources.title: How is the light of a lighthouse magnified so that it can be seen many miles out at sea?

questions.verificationNotes: Fresnel lenses are a classic lighthouse solution; modern lights vary.

questions.question: What gave the original computer mouse its animal-like nickname?
questions.explanation: The mouse was named for its rodent-like shape and a cable resembling a tail.
questions.verificationNotes: Nickname refers to early cabled designs, not later wireless mice.

questions.question: Which animal may sleep buried in sand rather than in a nest or bed?
questions.explanation: NOAA describes Pacific sand lances burying themselves in sand to rest.
questions.verificationNotes: A specific fish example; fish do not all sleep the same way.

questions.question: What was the first practical computer mouse prototype made from instead of today’s plastic?
questions.explanation: The Computer History Museum preserves Douglas Engelbart’s early SRI mouse prototype made with a wooden body.
questions.verificationNotes: This refers to a surviving early prototype, not all later mice.

questions.question: What food is actually a fibrous fruit, although its name makes it sound like a nut?
questions.explanation: Botanically a coconut is a fibrous one-seeded drupe, though it is commonly called a nut.

sources.title: Is a coconut a fruit, nut or seed?

questions.verificationNotes: The precise botanical classification is a drupe, not a true nut.

questions.question: What surprising material can a beautiful white cloud contain in the hundreds of tons?
questions.explanation: Even small individual cloud droplets can add up to enormous quantities of water when spread through a large cloud.
questions.verificationNotes: Cloud water can be liquid droplets or ice; question is about bulk material, not a single droplet.

questions.question: At a quirky annual Finnish celebration, where is the official Sleepy Head of the Year thrown to wake them up?
questions.explanation: Naantali’s Sleepy Head Day features an honorary sleepy head being thrown into the Baltic Sea early in the morning.
questions.verificationNotes: A staged local festival ritual, not involuntary punishment for everyday lateness.

questions.question: Which country has a volcanic lake called Segara Anak, a name meaning “Child of the Sea”?
questions.explanation: Segara Anak is the crater lake within the Rinjani volcanic complex on Lombok, Indonesia.
questions.verificationNotes: The named lake is within a volcanic caldera on Lombok.

questions.question: What architectural feature can make you forget why you went into another room?
questions.explanation: A series of memory experiments found that passing through a doorway can function as an event boundary and impair immediate recall.

sources.title: Walking through doorways causes forgetting, new research shows

questions.verificationNotes: Other studies find the effect varies; this refers to particular task conditions.

questions.question: What awkward part of a nineteenth-century boot was the early zipper intended to replace?
questions.explanation: Whitcomb Judson designed an early clasp-locker to replace time-consuming boot laces.
questions.verificationNotes: The product evolved substantially before modern reliable zippers.

questions.question: Which plant can produce a single flower-like structure taller than many people?
questions.explanation: The titan arum, often called the corpse flower, produces one of the largest unbranched flower clusters in the world, reaching heights of about three metres.

sources.title: 16 weird plants that seem more supernatural than natural

questions.verificationNotes: The giant display is an inflorescence (a cluster of flowers), not one single botanical flower; its size is the point of this question.

questions.question: What type of pollution covered London so densely in December 1952 that people could barely see down streets?
questions.explanation: A temperature inversion trapped coal smoke and other pollutants in the deadly Great Smog of 1952.
questions.verificationNotes: The disaster included fog plus air pollution; not simply harmless natural fog.

questions.question: What agricultural leftover can be tightly baled and used to build the walls of a real home?
questions.explanation: Properly compacted, protected straw bales have been used to make durable building walls.

sources.title: Can you really build a house with straw?

questions.verificationNotes: Dry, detailed straw-bale construction, not loosely piled straw.

questions.question: What kind of expensive 1950s kitchen appliance was originally sold using radar-derived heating?
questions.explanation: The early Tappan household microwave was an expensive mid-1950s appliance that used magnetron microwave heating.

sources.title: Tappan Model RL-1 Microwave Oven
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

questions.verificationNotes: The historical appliance is distinct from today’s low-cost compact microwaves.

questions.question: Which ocean animal can use its own jet propulsion to briefly glide above the sea?
questions.explanation: Some squid expel water in a jet, launch above the surface and spread fins and arms to glide.

sources.title: Fantastic flyers: 10 animals that fly in surprising ways

questions.verificationNotes: A gliding escape maneuver, not flight powered by wings.

questions.question: What real insect was found in a computer relay and taped into a 1947 engineering logbook?
questions.explanation: Engineers documented an actual moth lodged in a Harvard Mark II relay and attached it to the log.

sources.title: September 9: First Instance of Actual Computer Bug Being Found

questions.verificationNotes: The word computer bug was already in use; the moth did not coin the term.

questions.question: What food is often mistakenly labeled a “yam” in American supermarkets?
questions.explanation: North American groceries sometimes call varieties of sweet potato yams, despite true yams belonging to a different plant family.

sources.title: What is the difference between sweet potatoes and yams?

questions.verificationNotes: Regional retail naming differs from botanical identification.

questions.question: What item have astronauts said smells like gunpowder or hot metal after a spacewalk?
questions.explanation: Astronauts have described a distinctive metallic or gunpowder-like odor on their suits and tools once they return to the spacecraft.
questions.verificationNotes: The smell is noticed after re-entering the cabin; vacuum itself cannot be sniffed. Other exposed equipment may carry the odor.

questions.question: Which European country shares the Caribbean island of Saint Martin with the Netherlands?
questions.explanation: The island of Saint Martin is split between a French part and a Dutch part.
questions.verificationNotes: The French portion is Saint-Martin, and the Dutch portion is Sint Maarten; the whole island is shared.

questions.question: What do Venus flytraps detect to decide when to snap their traps shut?
questions.explanation: Sensitive trigger hairs inside a Venus flytrap register movements of a potential insect meal.

sources.title: 16 weird plants that seem more supernatural than natural

questions.verificationNotes: The trap does not snap merely from the plant smelling an insect.
